# Essentials Folders

> Full-text documentation of Essentials Folders — a Zen Browser mod that turns the Essentials (pinboard) grid into folder tiles. Tabs stay ordinary Zen tabs: the mod never moves or deletes anything.

## What it is

Essentials Folders is a browser mod for Zen Browser (1.24b and newer). It replaces the
Essentials grid — the pinboard panel that normally shows a flat row of pinned tabs — with
folder tiles. Each tile carries an icon, a name, a colour and a counter of how many tabs are
inside.

Clicking a tile opens the folder: the tile leaves the top row and unfolds into a wide plane of
its own colour, and that folder's tiles sit inside the plane. There is no separate header and
no duplicated tile — the folder is shown exactly once. Several folders can be open at the same
time, and the one you opened most recently sits above the others.

Folders nest inside each other to any depth, and both folders and tiles are rearranged by
ordinary mouse drag & drop. A nested folder keeps no header and no colour plane of its own: it
stays a tile in the row under its parent, and when it is open its icons appear as a dense strip
right under that row, inside the parent's colour plane. The open nested folder is underlined with
its own colour, and the strip of its icons carries a thin line of the same colour on the left.

## Features

- Folder tiles in the Essentials grid: icon, name, colour, tab counter.
- An open folder is a colour plane holding its own tiles. No duplication.
- The newest folder goes on top.
- Nested folders, unlimited depth, marked with a chevron.
- An open nested folder shows its icons in a dense strip under the row — it takes no block of its own.
- An expanded nested folder is marked: the chevron points down and the tile glows in the colour
  of the folder.
- The colour of a folder is set from its context menu (`Change colour…`); there is no strip over
  the panel.
- Drops are caught at the window level, before the browser's own handling: the target under the
  cursor is highlighted while you drag, and it is measured again at the moment of the drop —
  Zen shifts the Essentials grid while you drag, so the tile under the cursor moves.
  `window.__zenEssentialsFolders.lastDrop` holds the result of the last drop.
- A rule of a folder is matched with the address of a tab without regard to letter case, so
  an address with capitals in the path lands in the folder it was dropped into.
- A folder opens right after a tile is dropped into it, so the tile is not hidden under a
  closed lid. A tab dropped from the sidebar is made essential by the mod itself or by the
  browser, whichever can do it first. The rule of a folder follows the tab when it changes
  its address.
- Every option of the mod lives in its own preference, so the mod manager of Zen shows all
  22 of them, and a change made there is applied at once, without a restart. The mod shows
  its own version in the settings window.
- A tab dropped into a folder lands there even when the browser does not report the start of
  the drag: the drag is recognised by the drag data, and the folder that was highlighted while
  dragging is the one the tab goes into.
- A tab dropped into a folder lands in the folder that was highlighted while dragging, even if
  the grid moved and another tile ended up under the cursor.
- Rearranging folders by dragging a tile by its edge; rearranging tiles inside a folder by
  dragging an icon next to another icon.
- Only the dragged tab moves: drop one GitHub tab into another folder and only that tab goes,
  the other GitHub tabs stay put.
- Dropping onto the coloured area of an open folder moves the tile into that folder.
- Dragging a tab from the sidebar into a folder works too — the mod reads the tab straight
  from the drag buffer.
- A separator below the folders holds pinned tabs that are in no folder.
- Right-click menu on a tile: expand/collapse, open all tabs, pin to top, rename, change icon,
  change colour, nest into another folder, move to the top level, list sites, delete,
  expand/collapse all.
- A `+` tile at the end of the row creates a new folder.
- Search box above the tiles: filters by folder name or domain, `Esc` resets it.
- A pinned folder always stays in the top row, marked with a dot.
- The folder panel is height-limited and scrolls on its own; the regular Zen tab list and tab
  groups stay below it.
- Any colour for a folder: 16 presets, a colour picker, a `#rrggbb` field and a Random button.
- Bigger, brighter logos in the Essentials grid (26 px), all in identical cells so they line up.
- The active folder — the one holding the current tab — is marked with a glowing frame, a dot,
  a corner or a star. Pulsing can be switched off.
- The mod's own settings dialog: 22 options in five groups, applied immediately.

## Settings

The dialog opens with the `⚙` gear to the right of the search row, or with `Mod settings…` in
the folder menu.

| Group | What it controls |
|---|---|
| Folder tiles | tile height, minimum width, folder icon size, show names and counters, counter style (badge / dot / off), nesting chevron (on / off) |
| Icon grid | icon step inside a folder, logo size in Essentials, sidebar tab icon size, padding under a plane and the gap between blocks, tile row (strip / grid) |
| Indicators | active-folder style (glow / dot / corner / star), pulsing on/off and speed, unloaded-tab marker (frame / dashed / dot / line / dimmed / off) |
| Behaviour | search row, `+` button, hints for a failed drop, newest folder always on top |

Values apply immediately — there is nothing to save. `Reset` restores the defaults.

The five original preferences (`show-names`, `show-count`, `show-search`, `icon-size`,
`tab-icon-size`) still work: the mod reads an old value if you had one and keeps the new one
next to it, all in a single `zen.essentialsfolders.settings` pref.

## How membership works

A folder stores rules, not tabs. A plain rule is a domain: `github.com` means "every GitHub tab
in this folder". When you drag a tab from one folder to another, the mod remembers it more
precisely, by full URL.

| Rule | What lands in the folder |
|---|---|
| `github.com` | every GitHub tab |
| `github.com/owner/repo` | that repository and its inner pages |
| `github.com/` | only the GitHub home page |
| `!github.com/owner/repo` | nothing: that tab is excluded from the folder |

Dragging one `github.com/owner/repo` tile from "GitHub" into "Work" gives "Work" the rule
`github.com/owner/repo` (only that tab) and leaves "GitHub" with `github.com` plus the
exclusion `!github.com/owner/repo`. The remaining GitHub tabs stay where they were.

## Installation

The mod installs in a minute: ready-made files, no build step, no npm. Zen reads the mod at
startup, so restart Zen after installing.

Through Sine (the mod manager built into Zen):

1. Open `Settings` → `Sine Mods` → `Marketplace` in Zen.
2. Find **Essentials Folders** and press `Install`.
3. Restart Zen.

Or without the store: `Sine Mods` → `Install from repo`, then paste

    https://github.com/danonchek51/zen-essentials-folders

Manually: close Zen, copy `theme.json`, `preferences.json`, `chrome.css` and
`essentials-folders.uc.js` into `<Zen profile>\chrome\sine-mods\zen-essentials-folders\`, add
an entry to `chrome\sine-mods\mods.json`, and start Zen. `python install.py` does this for
you. Close Zen before editing `mods.json` and `prefs.js` — it rewrites them on exit.

## Where folders are stored

The data lives in the Zen preferences, so it survives restarts and browser updates:

- `zen.essentialsfolders.folders` — folders: name, colour, icon, parent (`parentId`), domains
  (`sites`) and their order, plus the `pinned` flag
- `zen.essentialsfolders.collapsed` — which folders are collapsed
- `zen.essentialsfolders.order` — the order of open folders, newest first
- `zen.essentialsfolders.settings` — the mod settings (one JSON)

A tab belongs to a folder by an address rule, not by tab id: a browser restart, a page
redirect and a tab move never break it.

## FAQ

**What is Essentials Folders?** A Zen Browser mod that turns the Essentials grid into folder
tiles, with nesting, drag & drop, search and 22 settings.

**Do I have to move my tabs into folders by hand?** No. The mod never moves or deletes
anything: tabs stay ordinary Zen tabs. Tabs join a folder by an address rule.

**Where does the mod save my folders?** In the Zen preferences (`zen.essentialsfolders.*`),
so they survive restarts and browser updates.

**Will the mod keep working after Zen updates?** Yes. It uses public Zen APIs
(`gZenWorkspaces.getCurrentEssentialsContainer()`) and the `.zen-essentials-container` CSS
class, and the DOM observer reconnects itself.

**Does it work with other mods?** Yes. It does not touch tabs or their data. Confirmed
compatibility: the Zen Tab Groups mod (oom333).

**Do I have to configure anything?** No, it works out of the box. The `⚙` gear opens 21
options in four groups if you want them.

**How do I undo the install?** Delete the `chrome\sine-mods\zen-essentials-folders` folder and
its entry in `mods.json`, then restart Zen. No tab is lost.

**The tiles are gone — what now?** Open `about:support` → "Profile Folder" and check that
`chrome\sine-mods\zen-essentials-folders\essentials-folders.uc.js` is there. Reloading Zen
with `Ctrl+Shift+R` often helps.

## Safety

The mod never moves and never deletes anything: tabs remain ordinary Zen tabs, so `Ctrl+W`
(unload), clicking the icon to reload and tab drag & drop keep working. It only draws its own
tiles into the Essentials grid, hides the contents of a collapsed folder and sets the display
order through CSS `order`. Zen's Essentials counter keeps counting real tabs only.
